mcqs.q: In dogs with terminal distemper, how did serum creatinine compare to healthy controls?
mcqs.e: Creatinine was significantly lower in the distemper group, likely reflecting reduced muscle mass.

mcqs.q: Which immunoglobulin was most frequently deposited in renal tissue of distemper dogs?
mcqs.e: IgM deposition was found in 92.3% of distemper cases.

mcqs.q: What did the study conclude about the kidneys in terminal canine distemper?
o: Genuine glomerular and tubular alterations are present
mcqs.e: Glomerular and tubular lesions were confirmed in 84.6% of animals, confirming renal alterations in terminal distemper.

mcqs.q: What was the effect of the intranasal B. bronchiseptica vaccine on olfactory performance in the follow-up study?
o: No effect on odor threshold or search time
mcqs.e: Neither odor threshold nor time spent searching was affected by the intranasal vaccine.

mcqs.q: Which factor most influenced detection dogs' time to find the target odor?
mcqs.e: Behaviors tied to positive and negative motivation affected search time, suggesting behavior must be considered in olfactory studies.

mcqs.q: What did the authors call the predominant CDV lineage circulating in Ontario wildlife?
mcqs.e: The predominant lineage, Canada-1, had not been previously described and is distinct from but most similar to America-1.

mcqs.q: Which species appeared important for maintaining and transmitting heterogeneous CDV lineages in Ontario?
mcqs.e: Raccoons appear to play an important role in maintenance and transmission of the co-circulating lineages.

mcqs.q: What avenue did the study suggest could introduce novel CDV lineages?
mcqs.e: An imported dog carried a non-local lineage, implicating travel/trade as a route for novel CDV introduction.

mcqs.q: Among CDV-positive dogs in the Galapagos outbreak, which clinical signs predominated?
mcqs.e: Respiratory signs occurred in 82.2% of positive dogs, more than neurological (48.8%) or GI (28.9%).

mcqs.q: Despite dog control and vaccination policies, CDV was concluded to remain a threat to which endangered species?
mcqs.e: The study emphasized CDV's continued threat to the endemic, endangered Galapagos sea lion.

mcqs.q: What was the CDV seroprevalence among free-roaming dogs around Chitwan National Park?
mcqs.e: Overall seroprevalence indicating past CDV exposure was 80.0%.

mcqs.q: How did age relate to CDV seroprevalence?
mcqs.e: Adult dogs showed significantly higher seroprevalence than juveniles, a finding that held on multivariable analysis.

mcqs.q: Why is free-roaming dog CDV exposure a conservation concern in this region?
o: Dogs may be a source of infection for susceptible wildlife like Bengal tigers
mcqs.e: Free-roaming dogs around the park could serve as a CDV source for susceptible wildlife such as the Bengal tiger.

mcqs.q: What was the pooled CaHV-1 seroprevalence in North Queensland dogs?
mcqs.e: Pooled seroprevalence across household and show dogs was 13%.

mcqs.q: Which factors were associated with CaHV-1 seropositivity?
o: Recent conjunctivitis and involvement in breeding
mcqs.e: Dogs with conjunctivitis in the prior 3 months or involved in breeding were more likely to be seropositive.

mcqs.q: What did the study conclude about fungal dysbiosis as a cause of dermatophytosis in Persian cats?
o: Apart from M. canis, dysbiosis is unlikely to play a role
mcqs.e: Aside from M. canis itself, an underlying fungal dysbiosis was judged unlikely to drive the disease.

mcqs.q: Did Persian cats with dermatophytosis show decreased cutaneous fungal diversity?
mcqs.e: Affected Persian cats did not exhibit decreased fungal diversity.

mcqs.q: Which dermatophyte dominated among positive stray animals in Puerto Rico?
mcqs.e: 18 of 19 positive animals were infected with M. canis.

mcqs.q: How did dermatophyte positivity compare between symptomatic and asymptomatic strays?
o: Symptomatic animals were positive far more often
Asymptomatic animals were positive more often
mcqs.e: Asymptomatic animals were positive 36% of the time versus only 13.5% of those with lesions.

mcqs.q: How well did MALDI-TOF MS confirm the microscopically diagnosed dermatophytes?
mcqs.e: All 19 dermatophytes (100%) were confirmed by MALDI-TOF MS.

mcqs.q: What was the effect of delayed sample processing on M. canis fungal culture?
o: Overgrowth of contaminants and lower M. canis recovery
mcqs.e: Delayed processing was closely associated with contaminant overgrowth and reduced M. canis recovery.

mcqs.q: Within what window did samples retain low contamination and good M. canis recovery?
mcqs.e: Samples processed at 8 h and 24 h had less NDM invasion and higher M. canis recovery than 48-72 h.

mcqs.q: Compared with in-house fungal culture, how did the commercial qPCR perform?
mcqs.e: qPCR had ~74% sensitivity and ~98% specificity, making it less sensitive but more specific than previously reported.

mcqs.q: What did the authors recommend for diagnosing dermatophytosis and confirming cure?
o: Use a combination of complementary diagnostic tests
mcqs.e: They concluded diagnosis and cure assessment should rely on a combination of complementary tests.

mcqs.q: Which body site was most commonly affected by T. mentagrophytes complex in these dogs?
mcqs.e: Lesions most often affected the muzzle (48%).

mcqs.q: How did ketoconazole, itraconazole, and terbinafine compare as systemic therapies?
mcqs.e: The three systemic antifungals appeared equivalent as treatment options.

mcqs.q: Which AKC group had the highest incidence of T. mentagrophytes complex infection?
mcqs.e: The Sporting group had the highest incidence (43%), followed by the Terrier group (20%).

mcqs.q: Which single strategy most substantially reduced modeled S. brasiliensis prevalence in cats?
mcqs.e: Mass treatment of infected cats substantially reduced prevalence, with effect amplified by adding neutering.

mcqs.q: What did the model conclude about contact-reduction methods used alone?
o: They are insufficient to reduce prevalence
mcqs.e: Contact-reduction methods alone were not sufficient to reduce sporotrichosis prevalence.
